staffing_plan.notes: Dedicated PM required for Phases 2-3 sprint cycles (R4 mitigation). Owns T2, T3, T4, T16, T23, T26, T27, T30. Must be 100% available for sprint planning, daily standups, and stakeholder feedback. Critical path tasks: T2, T3, T16, T26. No shared allocation.

Dedicated Backend Developer required for critical path tasks: T1, T6, T11, T21 (zero slack). Owns T1, T5, T6, T7, T9, T10, T11, T13, T15, T20, T24, T25, T28. Must be full-time Phases 1-4. Handles SSO integration (R1 de-risk), email scheduling (R2 de-risk), PagerDuty integration (R3 scope), codebase audit (R5 mitigation), and data retention (R7 mitigation). No shared allocation.
Owns T8, T12, T14. Has 2-4 days slack on UI tasks (T8, T12, T14). Can absorb minor delays without impacting critical path. Allocation 11.6% allows capacity for other projects or support tasks.

Owns T17, T18, T19, T21, T22, T29. Critical path task: T21 (zero slack). QA effort = 108h / 247h dev = 43.7% of backend dev hours, exceeds 25% minimum (PMBOK 8.2). Allocation 21.6% is sustainable. Must conduct comprehensive testing: email reliability (R2 mitigation), alert edge cases (R3 validation), regression suite (R5 validation), end-to-end integration (R6 mitigation), data retention compliance (R7 validation).

open_questions.question: Which SSO provider is in use (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, other), and is sandbox/test environment documentation and API access confirmed for the development team?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Authentication integration (T6, UC1) cannot proceed; blocks Phase 2 development start; 2-4 week timeline slip if provider docs incomplete or sandbox unavailable; potential re-architecture if provider does not support required grant flows (R1).

open_questions.question: Is an email service (SMTP, SendGrid, AWS SES, other) already provisioned and accessible, and what is its delivery SLA (target ≥99%)?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Email scheduling (T11, UC5) cannot proceed on schedule; if not provisioned, procurement delay 1-2 weeks; if SLA <99%, success metric '90% on-time delivery' becomes unachievable without service swap or metric re-negotiation (R2).

open_questions.question: For PagerDuty integration, are custom escalation policies, on-call schedule management, or incident lifecycle automation required, or is the scope limited to threshold-based alert triggering and notification?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Scope ambiguity on PagerDuty (T13, T14, T15, UC6, UC7) could add 40-60% backend effort if custom workflows required; discovered mid-Phase 2 causes rework and 1-2 week timeline slip (R3).

open_questions.question: Is the Product Manager confirmed as 100% dedicated to this project for Phases 2-3 (weeks 3-12), with no competing priorities or shared allocation?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Hybrid SDLC requires active PO engagement; undefined PM availability causes sprint planning delays, decision delays, and scope creep (R4). PM must own backlog prioritization and stakeholder feedback loops.

open_questions.question: What is the current state of the existing customer analytics dashboard codebase (test coverage %, technical debt inventory, architectural constraints affecting real-time refresh, alerting, email scheduling)?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Unknown codebase state could reveal integration complexity or refactoring needs not visible in brief; discovered during Phase 1 (T1) could compress Phase 2 timeline by 1-2 weeks (R5).

Assumption A2 (PagerDuty scope limited to threshold alerts) — MEDIUM risk if wrong; could add 40-60% backend effort
Assumption A3 (Email service provisioned with ≥99% SLA) — MEDIUM risk if wrong; blocks UC5 and success metric
SDLC approach is Hybrid — requires active PO engagement and adaptive sprint cycles; adds complexity vs. pure Waterfall
HIGH risk R1 (SSO integration) — critical path blocker if provider unavailable
HIGH risk R2 (Email service) — blocks UC5 and success metric if not provisioned
HIGH risk R3 (PagerDuty scope ambiguity) — could add 40-60% backend effort mid-Phase 2
HIGH risk R4 (PM availability) — Hybrid SDLC requires dedicated PO; undefined PM role causes sprint friction
HIGH risk R6 (Critical path schedule) — 12-week deadline with 4-person team and zero slack on critical path; no margin for integration issues or rework

pm_confidence_score.interpretation: PM confidence score is 62.0 because the project has well-defined requirements (HIGH input quality, Hybrid SDLC with predictive phase structure), a named 4-person team with direct stack experience, and clear success metrics. However, nine HIGH or MEDIUM risks create significant uncertainty: three critical external dependencies (SSO provider, email service, PagerDuty scope) are unconfirmed and could block Phase 2 development or add 40-60% backend effort if scope expands; PM availability is undefined despite Hybrid SDLC requiring active PO engagement; critical path has zero slack with 12-week deadline, leaving no margin for integration delays or rework; and codebase health is unknown. Confidence is further reduced by three assumptions (A1, A2, A3) with HIGH/MEDIUM risk if wrong. Mitigation: confirm all five open questions before Phase 2 kickoff, establish daily standup discipline for critical path tasks, and maintain 2-3 day buffer in Phase 3 for UAT rework.

project_viability.gap_description: Critical path duration (56 days = 11.2 weeks) is 93% of deadline (12 weeks). With 15% buffer applied in project plan, total duration is 12.88 weeks, exceeding deadline by 0.88 weeks (6.2 days). Project is AT_RISK if any critical path task slips >1 day or external dependencies (SSO, email, PagerDuty) are delayed.

scoping_options.title: Defer Phase 4 UAT and Load Testing to Post-Launch
scoping_options.description: Move T23 (UAT with CSMs), T25 (load testing) to post-launch backlog. Retain T24 (bug fixes), T26 (documentation), T27 (deployment checklist). Reduces Phase 4 from 2.5 weeks to 1.5 weeks. Total project duration: 11.88 weeks (within deadline). Risk: UAT feedback discovered post-launch may require hotfixes; load testing deferred increases production risk.

scoping_options.title: Reduce PagerDuty Integration Scope to MVP (Threshold Alerts Only)
scoping_options.description: Defer custom escalation policies, on-call automation, and advanced workflows to Phase 4 or post-launch. Reduces T13, T14, T15, T18 effort by 30% (12 hours). Reduces Phase 2 from 4.5 weeks to 4.2 weeks. Total project duration: 12.2 weeks (within deadline with 0.2-week buffer). Risk: Stakeholders may expect advanced PagerDuty workflows; scope creep if expectations not managed.

scoping_options.title: Add Contractor Backend Developer (0.5 FTE) for Phases 2-3
scoping_options.description: Hire contractor to support critical path backend tasks (T6, T11, T15, T20, T24, T25). Reduces Backend Developer allocation from 49.4% to 35%, freeing capacity for parallel task execution. Enables Phase 2 to compress from 4.5 weeks to 3.8 weeks. Total project duration: 11.3 weeks (within deadline with 0.7-week buffer). Cost: ~$15K-20K for 12-week contractor. Risk: Contractor onboarding (1 week), knowledge transfer overhead.
